questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.learningObjective: Apply improper integral comparison to solve a calculus problem.
questions.stem: Problem 1: Which technique correctly handles the improper integral comparison case with coefficient 1 in the beekeeper's logbook?

options.text: Increase the exponent by one, divide by that new exponent, and retain the constant of integration.
Decrease the exponent by one and multiply by the new exponent.
Divide by the old exponent and leave the exponent unchanged.
Multiply by the exponent and add one to the constant term.

questions.explanation: The correct rule applies the power rule with the constant multiple and sum rules, while distractors mishandle exponents or constants. Verify by differentiating the result.
questions.hint: Check which option differentiates back to the integrand.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.learningObjective: Apply definite integral evaluation to solve a calculus problem.
questions.stem: Problem 3: Explain why the power rule for antiderivatives requires adding one to the exponent in the beekeeper's logbook.

answer.exemplar: A correct solution increases the exponent by one, divides by the new exponent, retains the constant of integration, and verifies by differentiation.

questions.explanation: The power rule reverses differentiation: differentiating x^(n+1)/(n+1) returns x^n. Forgetting to add one leaves an exponent mismatch under differentiation.
questions.hint: Differentiate your candidate answer to recover the integrand.
